title: Tax-free refunds for purchases from November 2026
plain_summary: For purchases on or after November 1, 2026, eligible shoppers pay the tax-inclusive price and complete departure customs procedures before receiving the tax refund. Goods must leave Japan; retain the goods and purchase records. Customs requires the departure check within 90 days of purchase. Check purchaser eligibility, excluded goods and retailer refund arrangements before buying. A refund is not guaranteed.

title: Pocket Wi-Fi rental and coverage checks
plain_summary: Portable Wi-Fi routers are available through airport rental services and advance reservations. Compare the provider’s Japan coverage, data allowance, pickup or delivery, charging needs and return arrangements. TravelWifi lists Japan in its Global Rental Plan, but that list does not prove current inventory, delivery eligibility or reception along your route. Confirm the booking conditions directly.

title: Medical insurance and evacuation preparation
plain_summary: Before departure, check that your insurance covers treatment and unexpected medical evacuation for your Japan itinerary. Ask about exclusions, planned activities, how facilities are paid and how to reach insurer assistance. Do not assume a U.S. policy pays for overseas care or that cancellation cover includes medical treatment.

title: Finding care and paying for treatment
plain_summary: Medical treatment in Japan can be expensive. Facilities may check your insurance before treatment, and you should be prepared to pay. The FCDO links an English-speaking medical-provider directory. For prescriptions, U.S. prescriptions are not honored in Japan: plan supplies within Japanese import rules or arrange a local doctor. Pharmacy hours, stock and individual treatment require a local check.

title: Narita international arrival sequence
plain_summary: At Narita, follow the signs and staff instructions through applicable quarantine, immigration, baggage claim, plant or animal quarantine and customs before entering the arrivals lobby. Check the flight’s actual terminal and baggage display. These are Narita-specific procedures; they do not establish the layout of every Japanese airport.

title: Haneda terminal and onward transport
plain_summary: Haneda publishes terminal-specific routes from arrivals to trains, monorail, buses and taxis. Check the airport and terminal on your ticket, then select the onward connection for your actual destination and arrival time. Haneda is a Tokyo-area example, not an arrival instruction for all of Japan.

title: Narita buses and taxi transfers
plain_summary: Narita lists direct bus services to multiple destinations and airport ticket counters. Its taxis include standard and zone-based fixed-fare options to Tokyo; tolls and other charges may be additional. Use the official terminal pickup information and confirm destination, departure time and total fare. These details apply to Narita, not every airport or bus company.

title: Tokyo subway ticket coverage
plain_summary: The Tokyo Subway Ticket covers Tokyo Metro and Toei Subway lines for its stated 24-, 48- or 72-hour period from first use within the ticket’s validity conditions. It does not imply coverage of JR or every airport train. Check the route, eligible purchase method and current ticket conditions before buying.

title: Taxi payment and destination checks
plain_summary: Japanese taxis can be useful where public transport is inconvenient. Some accept cards, but not all; carry a suitable payment backup and show the destination clearly. For an airport transfer, use that airport’s official taxi information and confirm total charges rather than assuming a nationwide fare or booking rule.

title: Earthquake and weather alert preparation
plain_summary: Japan has earthquake, tsunami and severe-weather risks. Learn the evacuation instructions at your accommodation and stations, monitor Japan Meteorological Agency warnings and follow local authorities, including evacuation orders. Check seasonal conditions for your travel dates. This is preparedness guidance, not a prediction or an active alert.

title: Solo travel and nightlife precautions
plain_summary: Get local advice about places requiring extra caution. Keep belongings in sight, do not follow street touts into bars, watch your drinks and check prices before ordering. For a visitor, carry your passport; residents may use their Japanese residence card. Plan your return route and follow local warnings. These precautions are not a guarantee of safety.

title: Tipping customs and exceptions
plain_summary: Tipping is generally not customary in Japanese restaurants, bars, cafes, taxis or hotels. A private guide or interpreter accustomed to overseas visitors may accept a discreet gratuity, but it is not expected. Check the actual arrangement rather than applying a standard percentage.

title: Visit Japan Web and arrival documents
plain_summary: Visit Japan Web supports online immigration and customs arrival procedures. Use the official service and current instructions for your trip, and keep the required passport and immigration documents available. Online registration is a preparation tool; it does not itself establish permission to enter Japan.

title: Japan Rail Pass coverage and train conditions
plain_summary: The Japan Rail Pass is offered by the six JR Group companies. Check its eligible services and current purchase and reservation conditions against your itinerary. NOZOMI and MIZUHO use has additional conditions, including a special ticket for pass holders. A JR pass does not establish coverage of every private railway, subway or bus; compare the actual journeys before buying.

title: Yen and backup payment preparation
plain_summary: Japan uses the yen (JPY). Carry some yen as well as another suitable payment method, especially for smaller businesses and rural stays. Check the current exchange rate and conversion costs when exchanging; a static USD-to-yen figure is not a current quote.

title: ATM access and withdrawal costs
plain_summary: Not every ATM accepts every overseas card, and access hours and withdrawal fees vary. Check your card issuer’s overseas withdrawal rules and the ATM’s displayed fees before confirming. Keep enough yen for times or places where a compatible cash machine is unavailable.

title: Payment cards and Suica or PASMO
plain_summary: Check the payment logos at the actual business; card acceptance does not eliminate the need for cash. Suica, PASMO and other compatible IC cards can pay on supported transport and at participating shops. Coverage, purchase, refund and top-up rules vary by card and operator. Do not assume an overseas mobile wallet works with every Japanese terminal.

title: SIM and eSIM device checks
plain_summary: Before using a different carrier, check that your phone is unlocked and supports the chosen SIM or eSIM plan. Confirm Japan coverage, activation, data allowance, validity and whether calls or texts are included; check home-carrier roaming charges too. Apple’s linked instructions apply to compatible iPhones; for other devices, use the manufacturer’s and carrier’s instructions.

sources.title: eSIM during international travel on iPhone

title: Airport and accommodation Wi-Fi
plain_summary: Japan’s major international airports offer terminal Wi-Fi, with connection instructions varying by airport. Confirm Wi-Fi at your accommodation before booking, especially outside large city hotels. Public hotspots may need registration and may be slow or patchy; keep another way to reach your itinerary and contacts.

title: Device labels and voltage conversion
plain_summary: Japan uses 100-volt AC, with 50 Hz in the east and 60 Hz in the west. Check each appliance’s voltage and frequency rating and its manufacturer’s instructions before connecting it. A physical plug adapter does not change voltage; devices that are not compatible may need appropriate conversion equipment or should be left at home.

title: CDC vaccine planning for Japan
plain_summary: CDC advises a health visit at least a month before travel and staying current on routine vaccines and eligible COVID-19 vaccination. It says to consider hepatitis A for most travelers, with stronger recommendations for certain food and rural exposures. Hepatitis B is recommended for unvaccinated travelers under 60; older travelers may receive it. Review personal recommendations with a clinician. These are health recommendations, not blanket entry requirements.

title: Japanese encephalitis depends on itinerary
plain_summary: CDC recommends Japanese encephalitis vaccination for relocation, long stays or frequent visits to affected areas. Shorter visits may warrant discussion when rural or outdoor exposure increases risk. It is not recommended for short urban-only trips. Ask a clinician about your activities and accommodation rather than deciding from duration alone.

title: Measles notice and practical health precautions
plain_summary: CDC’s Japan page links a global measles notice, not a declaration of a Japan-specific outbreak. Check MMR protection under CDC’s international-travel recommendations. Also prevent insect bites and avoid contaminated floodwater; vaccination does not prevent every travel illness.

title: Onsen bathing and tattoo rules
plain_summary: Wash before entering a shared bath and keep towels and other items out of the water. Tattoo, clothing and access rules vary by facility: check directly before arrival. Some venues restrict tattoos, while others permit them or offer private baths. Do not assume either a universal ban or universal acceptance.

title: Identification and local conduct rules
plain_summary: Visitors should carry their passport; Japan residents may use their residence card. Local rules can differ from U.S. practice, including smoking restrictions and strict controls on medicines and drugs. Follow posted restrictions and check the relevant Japanese authority before bringing a controlled item. A U.S. prescription alone does not establish import permission.

title: Emergency numbers and visitor hotline
plain_summary: For an immediate emergency in Japan, call 110 for police or 119 for fire or ambulance. JNTO’s Japan Visitor Hotline is +81-50-3816-2787, available around the clock in English, Chinese and Korean for visitor assistance. It complements rather than replaces local emergency responders. Save your accommodation address and insurer assistance details before travel.

sources.title: Japan Visitor Hotline and emergency numbers

title: Shoes and shared-space etiquette
plain_summary: Remove shoes where requested and follow the facility’s directions about indoor and bathroom slippers. In traditional accommodation, check posted instructions and ask staff if uncertain. Bathing, dress and venue access rules vary, so use local instructions rather than assuming all venues follow identical customs.

title: Local and highway bus planning
plain_summary: Japan has local and longer-distance bus services. Choose the operator for your actual route and check stops, timetable, luggage and payment arrangements before departure. Use an IC card only where that service accepts it; do not assume a rail pass or another city’s fare rules apply.
